searchText: You can’t break at invalid because you can jump past it Yes, sure. In a simple way this works if "invalid" is spotted before any jump or there is not jumpdest after the "invalid". Any solidity contract with assert, such as the ones using early versions of SafeMath, will have JUMPDEST after INVALID Instead of break, you should scan to the next JUMPDEST Sorry, I confused the context. So I guess it is better to remove this check. Any reliable way of detecting the tailing data? Not in the general case The 2byte ABI used by the top trading contracts uses dynamic jumps
